quest.title: Ann, Mary-Ann, and Marionette
quest.description: Go to the hidden dwelling, place your tea table, and have Sandrone take a seat. Then, prepare to enjoy some tea with the guests...

talks.objective: Go to the hidden dwelling to start the tea party

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: To be honest, I'm still in shock.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You know, back then, both Alain and I thought you'd already left this world.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Hmm... If we had woken up earlier, maybe we could have visited you and Alain. But, I suppose that's fate.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Ms. Mary-Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Fate works in mysterious ways. Who would have thought that Ann and I would see a film poster featuring your portrait during our travels?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So that's what made you think to contact me?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Precisely!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Ah... The aroma of coffee. It really takes me back... Hehe, thank you for inviting us to your tea party, Miss Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Your garden is so elegantly arranged. It's perfect for a lady of such grace.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: This is the home Alain and I once shared. I feel it's only right that I maintain its beauty.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: See? You're already so much better at this than my brother.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Alain never even decorated his room. He couldn't deal with pretty things.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: That's right, and Rene was no different. Jakob and I were the only ones who could properly spruce up a room — and prepare a tea party.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So he was like that even when he was little? I always thought it was due to his age...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: He was always that way. He may have been book smart, but he was a bit of a klutz in other ways.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Maybe that's why he was the only one of us who chose painful reality over the illusion of a sweet dream.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh. I don't think he regretted that choice.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: No, because that was his wish as a hero.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The regret is ours. His wish should never have stood alone.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: What about you, Miss Sandrone? Is there something you wish for?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alain once asked me that exact same question.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Hmm? So he asked you that, too?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: My brother must have matured a lot. He never would have asked something like that when I knew him.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "Wish" is such a hollow word. Can you ever have whatever you want? Hah, if that were the case, there would be no bad in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'm doing what I want to do, what I believe to be right. I don't know if this counts as a wish, but it makes me happy.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Hmm, now that is a wonderful thing. I envy you.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Then do you... resent Alain? Because he created you... in Mary-Ann's image.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Never. He always made it clear that I'm my own person — unique and distinct — and that I should choose my own life. So that's exactly what I did.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Haha, whether it's stories or food, as long as you're happy with your choices, then they're the right choices for you, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Exactly. So now, let's just quietly enjoy the food you've so carefully prepared for us.

talks.objective: Go to the hidden dwelling to start the tea party

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Life is best when all is peaceful and calm...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Let's sit like this for a little while longer.)

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Is that the time? Haha. We should get together more often, Miss Sandrone.
